title: set_once_with_fallback hardcodes provider=google inside a provider-agnostic flow
detail: complete_oauth_flow is provider-agnostic (it never learns the provider), yet the fallback hardcodes google. Correct only while allowed_oauth_providers stays ["google"]; a second provider silently misattributes every OAuth signup as google.
recommended_fix: Pass the provider into set_once_with_fallback (derive from the initiate request or token response) or read it from the query; default to google only while the allowlist is single-entry.

title: first-touch cookie max-age is a second literal mirroring pkce_max_age, coupled by comment only
evidence:
server/src/auth/first_touch_cookie.gleam:30:
  pub const max_age: Int = 300

server/src/auth/auth_handler.gleam:969:
  const pkce_max_age = 300

first_touch_cookie.gleam:24-26 (module docstring):
  /// The cookie is signed (server-only write/read), short-lived (same max-age
  /// as the PKCE verifier), and cleared on every terminal OAuth response.
detail: Two literals (300) in different modules are coupled by comment only. Changing pkce_max_age lengthens/shortens the PKCE window but leaves the first-touch cookie at 300 — stale attribution can outlive (or underlive) the flow it tags.
recommended_fix: Reference one constant: export pkce_max_age from auth_handler or move both windows into a shared auth module (e.g. pkce.gleam) and import it in first_touch_cookie.

title: Attribution key list triplicated (client extractor, signup_decoder, first_touch_cookie.keys) with no enforced sync
evidence:
server/src/auth/first_touch_cookie.gleam:35-43:
  const keys = [
    "utm_source",
    "utm_medium",
    "utm_campaign",
    "utm_content",
    "utm_term",
    "gclid",
    "fbclid",
    "msclkid",
  ]

server/src/auth/auth_handler.gleam:147-154 (signup_decoder):
  use utm_source <- decode.optional_field("utm_source", "", decode.string)
  use utm_medium <- decode.optional_field("utm_medium", "", decode.string)
  use utm_campaign <- decode.optional_field("utm_campaign", "", decode.string)
  use utm_content <- decode.optional_field("utm_content", "", decode.string)
  use utm_term <- decode.optional_field("utm_term", "", decode.string)
  use gclid <- decode.optional_field("gclid", "", decode.string)
  use fbclid <- decode.optional_field("fbclid", "", decode.string)
  use msclkid <- decode.optional_field("msclkid", "", decode.string)

client/src/helpers/first_touch.gleam (const keys):
  "utm_source", "utm_medium", "utm_campaign", "utm_content", "utm_term", "gclid",
  "fbclid", "msclkid",

first_touch_cookie.gleam:33-34: "/// Keys the first-touch cookie may carry — mirrors the client extractor
/// (`client/src/helpers/first_touch.gleam`) and the signup body decoder
detail: The attribution key list now lives in three places (client extractor, signup_decoder, first_touch_cookie.keys) joined only by comments. Adding a key to the decoder but not the cookie module silently drops OAuth attribution for it; no test pins them together.
recommended_fix: Define the key list once (attribution.gleam, imported by first_touch_cookie) and add a unit test asserting cookie keys == signup body keys; client copy stays duplicated only because of the JS/Erlang target split.
